change.title: @google/generative-ai (npm) is deprecated and reaches end of life; migrate to @google/genai

source.quote: All support for this repository (including bug fixes) will permanently end on **November 30, 2025**.

tasks.reasoning:
pnpm-lock pins @google/generative-ai 0.24.1, which falls inside the affected range (<=0.24.1). All support, including bug fixes, ended 2025-11-30. The fix is to replace the package with @google/genai at the latest version (>=2.0.0). Port each getGenerativeModel/generateContent call to ai.models.generateContent({model, contents, config}) and update the response handling (response.text is a property in @google/genai). The code scan did not read how responses are handled, so the migration agent must check each call site. Usage 4 (raw HTTP in match-teams) does not use the SDK and is not part of this move.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- gemini:genai-js-0x-breaking-0-9-0 (sdk-major): @google/genai (npm) 0.9.0 (0.x): generateContent contents parameter types simplified (also 0.7.0 File.sizeBytes number to string, 0.5.0 turnComplete default true, 0.3.0 file.upload named params), effective 2025-04-17. The repo does not use @google/genai yet. These 0.x changes (simplified generateContent contents types, File.sizeBytes as string, named file.upload params) only matter when porting calls into @google/genai. The port should write generateContent calls against the current simplified types, so no separate edit is needed.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/js-genai/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Simplified the types allowed on the generateContent contents parameter."
- gemini:genai-js-2-0-0-interactions (sdk-major): @google/genai (npm) 2.0.0: breaking Interactions API changes (steps replace outputs, new response_format, renamed SSE events); GenerateContent unaffected, effective 2026-05-07. The migration targets the current @google/genai (2.x). Its breaking changes are confined to the Interactions API, which this repo does not use ('GenerateContent usage in unaffected'). The only consequence is choosing >=2.0.0 as the target version, which is part of this move.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/js-genai/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Note: The breaking changes are only in interactions. `GenerateContent` usage in unaffected."

callSites.why: Uses the deprecated @google/generative-ai 0.24.1 getGenerativeModel; must be ported to @google/genai (ai.models.generateContent).
Uses the deprecated @google/generative-ai getGenerativeModel with generationConfig; config moves to the `config` field of generateContent in @google/genai.

## @google/generative-ai (npm) is deprecated and reaches end of life; migrate to @google/genai [Verified]

### Change

Replaced @google/generative-ai with @google/genai ^2.0.0 (resolved 2.32.0) via pnpm. Ported four call sites (chat route, ai-client, ai-utils, ai-advanced-utils) to `new GoogleGenAI({apiKey})` and `ai.models.generateContent({model, contents, config})`. Responses now read `result.text`. The generationConfig in ai-client moved to `config`. Added scripts/check-genai-migration.mjs. Typecheck and build pass.

Files touched:
- `app/api/ai/chat/route.ts`
- `lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts`
- `lib/ai-client.ts`
- `lib/ai-utils.ts`
- `package.json`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- `scripts/check-genai-migration.mjs`

### Why

The old SDK is end-of-life as of 2025-11-30 and its getGenerativeModel/response.text() API doesn't exist in @google/genai.

> All support for this repository (including bug fixes) will permanently end on **November 30, 2025**.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/generative-ai-js/HEAD/README.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| genai-migration | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- genai-migration, added by the agent: `export DATABASE_URL='postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/buddy_connect' JWT_SECRET='placeholder-secret-for-build' NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL='http://localhost:3000'; node scripts/check-genai-migration.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Before the baseline the harness ran `npx prisma generate` (Prisma client (prisma-client-js) is generated by the postinstall step, which was skipped; @prisma/client types and the build need it. Prisma 7 config may need a DATABASE_URL placeholder, but generate does not connect.); it exited 0.
- Checks ran with placeholder env: DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL.

Test of this change: `genai-migration`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- No runtime test of the actual generateContent calls (mocked provider). The proof test is static plus an SDK shape check.
- 0.9.0 contents-type changes: calls pass a plain string as `contents`, which is the current simplified type. No other edit was needed.
- 2.0.0 Interactions breaking changes: the repo does not use the Interactions API, so none apply.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- `result.text` is `string | undefined` in the new SDK. The utils files use `?? ""` so an empty response is handled as before. ai-client still throws on empty text.
- The new SDK may throw different error types or messages. Timeout handling in ai-client is unchanged: the AbortController there was never wired to the request, and that is unchanged.

---

review.summary: The port reaches every named call site: route.ts, ai-client.ts, and all 9 functions in each of ai-utils.ts and ai-advanced-utils.ts. It maps generationConfig to config correctly in ai-client.ts and drops the old package. The checks are only static (typecheck, build, and a grep script that builds a client with a dummy key), so no live request is proven. There is also one real behaviour change. The old SDK's `response.text()` threw on a blocked or empty candidate. The new `result.text` returns undefined, and the diff turns that into `""` with `?? ""`. In several places that silently replaces the old error or fallback path with an empty result. I could not confirm `@google/genai@2.32.0` from memory; check the npm registry and the SDK's types. A 'verified' grade overstates what the checks show.

concerns.issue: Line ~57: `result.text ?? ""` means a safety-blocked or empty response now returns 200 `{success: true, message: ""}`. Previously `response.text()` threw and the route returned a 500 'Failed to generate response'. The client may now render an empty assistant bubble.

`improvePostContent` (~line 157) used to fall back to the original `postContent` when the model response was blocked, because the throw was caught. Now it returns `""`, which could wipe the user's post if the caller replaces the content with the result. `generateNetworkingAdvice` changes the same way, though its catch already returned `""`, so that one only loses the console.error.

`optimizeProfileSummary` (~line 133) used to return the original `bio` on a blocked response. It now returns `""`, which could clear a user's bio. `generateNetworkingStrategy` and `generateSalaryNegotiationGuide` now return empty strings silently with no error log.

The module-level `new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY || "" })` runs at import time with an empty key when the env var is unset. Confirm two things: that the new constructor does not throw on an empty key (that would break any route importing this module, unlike the old SDK), and whether it silently falls back to GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY from the environment. The same applies to lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts.

The AbortController in generateWithTimeout is still never wired to the request, so the timeout is a no-op. This was already true before the change. The new SDK may accept an abort signal in `config` (I could not confirm the field name), so this is a cheap point to fix it. Not a regression.

The check is a static grep plus `typeof ai.models.generateContent === 'function'`. It does not exercise a request, response parsing, config mapping, or error handling. Typecheck passing does not prove runtime parity for the blocked or empty-response paths above.
I could not confirm that `@google/genai@^2.32.0` exists or what its API surface is; check npm and the package's .d.ts. Its `engines >=20.0.0` is compatible with the repo's `>=20.11.0`.

checkFirst: Decide whether blocked or empty model output should throw (old behaviour) or return `""`. In particular, restore the original-text fallback in improvePostContent and optimizeProfileSummary.
Confirm that `new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: "" })` does not throw at import time, and check whether it falls back to other env keys.
Run one live request against each entry point (chat route, ai-client generateContent with temperature/maxOutputTokens, one ai-utils function) using a real AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY.
Verify the @google/genai version and the `text` getter semantics in the SDK's type definitions.

change.title: gemini-2.0-flash and flash-lite models shut down June 1 2026

source.quote: The following Gemini 2.0 models are now [shut down](/docs/deprecations):

tasks.reasoning:
gemini-2.0-flash was shut down on 2026-06-01 and is named directly at three call sites. The AI chat, utility and matching features will error outright. Replace it with a currently supported model, ideally a single constant shared by every site. Do not choose gemini-2.5-flash or gemini-2.5-pro: they are deprecated and reroute on 2026-12-01. Also avoid gemini-3.5-flash and gemini-3.7-flash, which are deprecated and auto-routed. If the new model is Gemini 3.6+, remove temperature/top_p/top_k from generationConfig in lib/ai-client.ts. Two things are uncertain and need checking: the modelName default in lib/ai-client.ts and the model segment in the match-teams URL.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- gemini:2026-07-21-sampling-params-deprecated (field-removed): Sampling parameters temperature, top_p, top_k deprecated for Gemini 3.6+ models, effective 2026-07-21. temperature/top_p/top_k are deprecated only for Gemini 3.6+ models. They bite only if the replacement for gemini-2.0-flash is a 3.6+ model and lib/ai-client.ts generationConfig sets sampling params. Handle this in the same model-replacement edit.
  Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog.md.txt
  "The sampling parameters `temperature`, `top_p`
and `top_k` are now deprecated."

callSites.why: Hardcodes model "gemini-2.0-flash", which is shut down; requests fail.
Model comes from modelName (value not captured by the scan); likely defaults to gemini-2.0-flash like the rest of the repo. Verify and replace.
Raw POST to generativelanguage.googleapis.com with a runtime-built URL; it probably embeds a model name such as gemini-2.0-flash. Verify and replace.

## gemini-2.0-flash and flash-lite models shut down June 1 2026 [Verified]

### Change

Replaced retired gemini-2.0-flash with gemini-2.5-flash-lite via a shared GEMINI_MODEL constant (lib/ai-model.ts) used in chat route, ai-utils, ai-advanced-utils, ai-client default modelName, and match-teams. In match-teams, the model list (2.0-flash, 1.5-flash, 1.5-pro) is now just `models/${GEMINI_MODEL}`. Added scripts/check-gemini-model.mjs as proof.

Files touched:
- `app/api/ai/chat/route.ts`
- `app/api/hackathon/match-teams/route.ts`
- `lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts`
- `lib/ai-client.ts`
- `lib/ai-model.ts`
- `lib/ai-utils.ts`
- `scripts/check-gemini-model.mjs`

### Why

gemini-2.0-flash was shut down 2026-06-01, so every call would fail. gemini-2.5-flash and 3.5/3.7-flash are deprecated or rerouted, so I chose gemini-2.5-flash-lite, which is not deprecated.

> The following Gemini 2.0 models are now [shut down](/docs/deprecations):

Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog.md.txt

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| gemini-model-check | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- gemini-model-check, added by the agent: `export DATABASE_URL='postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/buddy_connect' JWT_SECRET='placeholder-secret-for-build' NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL='http://localhost:3000'; node scripts/check-gemini-model.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Before the baseline the harness ran `npx prisma generate` (Install scripts were off, so the Prisma client was never generated. The code imports @prisma/client, and tsc and next build need its generated types.); it exited 0.
- Checks ran with placeholder env: DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL.

Test of this change: `gemini-model-check`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Whether the match-teams REST fallback path (`/v1/models/...:generate`) is a valid endpoint was not touched; it looks pre-existing and likely wrong (generateContent expected).
- The @google-ai/generativelanguage `generateText` SDK path in match-teams is legacy and may not work with the new model.
- No provider validators were run (none apply to the SDK calls).
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Output tone, length and quality may differ with gemini-2.5-flash-lite versus 2.0-flash; review AI outputs.
- match-teams no longer falls back to retired gemini-1.5 models.
- Sampling-params deprecation (2026-07-21): not triggered. The replacement is not Gemini 3.6+, so temperature in lib/ai-client.ts generationConfig is kept. If the model is later moved to 3.6+, drop temperature/top_p/top_k there and in match-teams.
- gemini-2.5-flash-lite has no announced shutdown date, but may be retired later.

---

This route calls Gemini through the legacy PaLM-style surfaces: `TextGenerationClient.generateText` from @google-ai/generativelanguage, and REST `v1/models/...:generate` with a `{prompt:{text}}` body. As far as I know these never served Gemini models, which use generateContent. So the route likely fell through to the `openai/gpt-4-turbo` gateway fallback before this change and will keep doing so. Swapping the model name does not make this path call Gemini. The diff also cuts the fallback list from three models to one. That is harmless only because the 1.5 models are retired too.

Only the default `model` was changed. Any caller of `generateContent(prompt, { model: "gemini-2.0-flash" })` elsewhere in the repo would still hit the retired model. The new check script scans only the five named files, so it would not catch that. A repo-wide grep for `gemini-2.0` and `gemini-1.5` is needed.

Gemini 2.5 models support 'thinking'. If thinking tokens count against `maxOutputTokens` for this model, callers that pass small limits could get truncated or empty output. An empty response makes ai-client.ts throw 'Empty response from AI model', which triggers a retry and then returns null. I believe Flash-Lite has thinking off by default, but I could not confirm that for this SDK version.

record.prBody:
## Generate Content API: new paid-tier projects now store requests by default (store=true); opt out with store=false [Verified]

### Change

Ported the four Gemini SDK call sites from the deprecated @google/generative-ai to @google/genai (2.32.0) and set config.store=false on every generateContent call. Added lib/gemini-client.ts with a GEMINI_STORE=false constant and a small createModel helper that keeps the existing result.response.text() call sites unchanged. Ported lib/ai-client.ts directly. The raw REST fallback in match-teams was left alone.

Files touched:
- `app/api/ai/chat/route.ts`
- `lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts`
- `lib/ai-client.ts`
- `lib/ai-utils.ts`
- `lib/gemini-client.ts`
- `package.json`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- `scripts/check-gemini-store.mjs`

### Why

The source says new paid-tier projects now store requests by default (store=true). This repo sends chat and profile data through generateContent. The old SDK has no store field, so the port to @google/genai, where GenerateContentConfig.store exists, was needed to opt out.

> now store requests by default
> (`store=true`), matching the Interactions API.

Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog.md.txt

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| gemini-store-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- gemini-store-proof, added by the agent: `export DATABASE_URL='postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/buddy_connect' JWT_SECRET='placeholder-secret-for-build' NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL='http://localhost:3000'; node scripts/check-gemini-store.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Before the baseline the harness ran `npx prisma generate` (Prisma client is generated by postinstall, which was skipped; tsc and next build import @prisma/client types and need the generated client.); it exited 0.
- Checks ran with placeholder env: DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL.

Test of this change: `gemini-store-proof`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- app/api/hackathon/match-teams/route.ts REST fallback posts to the legacy v1 `:generate` endpoint with a prompt-style body (a different API from generateContent). It was not changed, and store was not added there.
- Whether the API key belongs to a new paid-tier project is unknown. store=false is sent regardless.
- Whether the live API accepts config.store on the Gemini Developer API for gemini-2.0-flash is untested. The type exists in the SDK.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Requests are sent with store=false, so Google does not retain them.
- Dependency swap: @google/generative-ai removed, @google/genai added. The lockfile was updated by pnpm.
- Empty responses now yield an empty string (result.text ?? "") instead of the old SDK's text() throwing on blocked content.

review.summary: The opt-out intent is sound, and the four `@google/generative-ai` call sites now send `config.store = false` through `lib/gemini-client.ts` or `lib/ai-client.ts`. But the PR swaps the whole SDK (`@google/generative-ai` 0.24 → `@google/genai` 2.32) to get there, which changes error and empty-response behaviour and key handling. The only new check is a source grep: it does not show that `store:false` reaches the request body. The fifth named call site (`match-teams`) is untouched and unexplained. The 'verified' grade overstates what the checks prove.

concerns.issue: `gemini-store-proof` only greps source text for `GEMINI_STORE = false` and `store: GEMINI_STORE`. It never builds a request or inspects the outgoing payload. Nothing proves that `@google/genai` 2.32 serialises `config.store` into the generateContent body (some config fields map to top-level request fields, others are client-only). Typecheck passing suggests `store` exists on `GenerateContentConfig`, but I could not confirm the wire mapping; check the SDK's request converters for `store`. A request-capture test is needed before 'verified' is justified.

Behaviour change beyond the API change. The old SDK's `response.text()` threw on blocked or empty candidates, so callers' catch blocks ran their fallbacks. The new wrapper returns `r.text ?? ""` silently. Examples: `improvePostContent` (`lib/ai-utils.ts`) and `optimizeProfileSummary` (`lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts`) will now return an empty string instead of the original post or bio. Several `ai-advanced-utils` functions will return an empty string instead of logging an error.

`createModel(process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY || "", ...)` runs at module load (same in `lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts`). The old SDK tolerated an empty key until call time. `new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: "" })` may either throw at import time or fall back to `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` env vars, silently using a different key or project. That project may not be the one the store opt-out was reasoned about. Verify the constructor's behaviour in 2.32.

This named call site is not touched. It uses the legacy `@google-ai/generativelanguage` `generateText` and REST `v1/{model}:generate`, not generateContent. The store default probably doesn't apply, but the PR should say so explicitly. If any of these paths reach a generateContent-backed endpoint, user names, skills and departments would be stored by default.

This is a full SDK migration to `@google/genai` ^2.32.0, plus new transitive deps (`p-retry`, `ws`, `protobufjs`, `google-auth-library`) and a `node >=20.0.0` engine. Retry, timeout and error semantics differ from the old SDK, and none of this is exercised by a live call. Consider whether a smaller change was possible, or call out the migration prominently.

Not a regression: the `AbortController` timeout still is not passed to the SDK, so `timeoutMs` never actually aborts the request. The rewrite was a natural moment to wire it in via the new SDK's abort option (I could not confirm the exact option name).

Check `@google/genai` 2.32 constructor behaviour with `apiKey: ""`: does it throw at import, or fall back to `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY`?
Decide whether returning an empty string on blocked or empty responses (vs. the old throw → fallback) is acceptable for `improvePostContent` and `optimizeProfileSummary`.
Confirm the `match-teams` legacy `generateText` / `v1:generate` paths are outside the store-default change, and note it in the PR.
Confirm against the quoted changelog or API reference that `store=false` is accepted for this project's tier and for `gemini-2.0-flash` (not rejected).
